verdict.summary: Create one OAuth app for many customers. A new app starts in Development status. Initially, only your developer account is authorized. Dropbox must approve production status before any number of users can link the app. Dropbox normally does not review a production request until 50 users have linked. You can request early review with evidence and a detailed reason.
verdict.activeEffort: About 4–5 hours for the listed setup, testing, webhook, and review-preparation work
verdict.waitTime: Dropbox publishes no standard review time. A 2015 community reply said a few business days. Normally, Dropbox does not review until 50 users have linked.
verdict.mainGate: Dropbox normally does not review a production request until the app has linked 50 users. Earlier review requires evidence and a detailed reason.

recommendation.text: Create one Dropbox Files API app with Full Dropbox access only when the agent needs existing customer files. Use OAuth authorization-code flow with offline access. Choose App folder if all work can stay inside `/Apps/<your app>`.

sources.quote: For non-Business API apps this can be either App folder or Full Dropbox.
Once your app is approved for production status, any number of Dropbox users can link to your app.
Dropbox supports both response_type=code and response_type=token . However, response_type=token is considered legacy and no longer recommended.
App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder).
If your app is scoped, webhooks require your app to have files.metadata.read authorized by the user

scopeTiers.need: Read metadata and work only inside the app's dedicated folder.

sources.quote: Full Dropbox: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on all data within the user’s Dropbox account.
The scope required for any given API call is documented on the endpoint:

scopeTiers.need: Discover files and read their contents across the customer's Dropbox.

sources.quote: Scopes are generally organized into major actions, often read and write, on major objects.
we’ll review that your app doesn’t request an unnecessarily broad permission based on the functionality provided by the app.

scopeTiers.need: Create, edit, move, or delete files in the customer's Dropbox.

essentials.text: Request `token_access_type=offline`. Store each customer's refresh token encrypted. Use the returned `expires_in` value. The documented sample is 14,400 seconds. Refresh tokens remain reusable until revoked.

sources.quote: then the access token payload returned by a successful /oauth2/token call will contain a short-lived access_token and a long-lived refresh_token
" expires_in " : 14400
This refresh token is long-lived and won’t expire automatically. It can be stored and re-used multiple times.

essentials.text: Register every callback on the OAuth 2 Settings tab. Send the exact registered URI in each authorization request. Use HTTPS except for localhost. Use one fixed callback and signed state.

sources.quote: This must be the exact URI registered under OAuth 2 on your app’s Settings tab in the Developer Console
This parameter should be used to protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

essentials.text: New apps start in Development status. Initially only the developer is authorized. Development apps can link 500 total users. At 50 linked users, Dropbox gives two weeks to obtain production approval before further linking freezes.

sources.quote: Initially, your new app will only be authorized for you.
It can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users.
Once your app links 50 Dropbox users, you will have two weeks to apply for and receive production status approval

essentials.text: No general numeric API limit was found. Handle HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`. Use exponential backoff, queues, and per-customer concurrency limits.

sources.quote: Dropbox may set and enforce limitations on Developer’s use of the DBX Platform, such as limiting the number of calls accepted by services on the DBX Platform, in its own discretion.

essentials.text: No API fee schedule or paid production tier was found in the researched terms. Production is described as a request and approval process.

sources.quote: To move a Developer App into production, or to gain access to certain features of the DBX Platform, Developer must submit a request for production status to Dropbox.

essentials.text: Move the app to production status before unrestricted customer connections. After approval, any number of Dropbox users can link the app.

sources.quote: Once your app is approved for production status, any number of Dropbox users can link to your app.

essentials.text: In Settings, select Apply for production. Add an icon first. Provide use-case details, compliant branding, and an app-specific privacy policy. Review normally begins only after 50 linked users.

sources.quote: click Apply for production in the App configuration section of your app’s Settings tab in the Developer Console
Before you apply, add an app icon on your app’s Branding tab.
it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users

essentials.text: Protect tokens with reasonable security controls. Support token values larger than 1 KB. Get clear user consent before sending file content to an external AI provider. For webhooks, verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature and answer within 10 seconds.

sources.quote: Applications must support variable token size with tokens capable of exceeding 1KB.
use and disclose User Data only as authorized by the User and only as necessary for the functionality of the Developer App.
Your app only has ten seconds to respond to webhook requests.

requests.text: Open this URL in the user's system browser; offline access returns a refresh token.

sources.quote: https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize
Method: GET

Example: Auth URL for PKCE code flow
https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id = <APP_KEY> & response_type = code & code_challenge =< CHALLENGE >& code_challenge_method =< METHOD >
If this parameter is set to offline, then the access token payload returned by a successful /oauth2/token call will contain a short-lived access_token and a long-lived refresh_token

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the authorization code using the PKCE verifier; the redirect URI must match the authorization request.

sources.quote: https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token
Method: POST

Example: PKCE code flow access token request
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \ 
    -d code= < AUTHORIZATION_COD E > \ 
    -d grant_type=authorization_code \ 
    -d redirect_uri= < REDIRECT_UR I > \ 
    -d code_verifier= < VERIFICATION_COD E > \ 
    -d client_id= < APP_KE Y >

redirect_uri String? The redirect URI used to receive the authorization code from /oauth2/authorize, if provided. Only used to validate it matches the redirect URI supplied to /oauth2/authorize for the current authorization code.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens
requests.curl:
curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token \
  -d code=AUTH_CODE \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID

requests.text: Use the long-lived refresh token to obtain a new short-lived access token.

sources.quote: https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token
Method: POST

Example: PKCE refresh token request
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token \ 
    -d grant_type=refresh_token \ 
    -d refresh_token= < REFRESH_TOKE N > \ 
    -d client_id= < APP_KE Y >
This refresh token is long-lived and won’t expire automatically. It can be stored and re-used multiple times.

requests.label: Refresh the access token
requests.curl:
curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID

requests.text: Call Dropbox's current-account endpoint with the bearer access token.

sources.quote:
curl -X POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/users/get_current_account \
 --header "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS TOKEN>"

requests.label: Check the connection

requests.text: Revoke the access token and its corresponding refresh token, if any.

sources.quote: Apps can revoke an access token (and corresponding refresh token, if any) using the /2/auth/token/revoke endpoint.
All other API requests are done via api.dropboxapi.com, content.dropboxapi.com, or notify.dropboxapi.com.

requests.label: Revoke access

detail.text: Open the DBX Platform Developer Console. Create a Files API app. Choose App folder or Full Dropbox based on the files the agent must access.

sources.quote: It walks you through three steps: choose an API, choose the type of access you need, and name your app.

detail.text: Open the Permissions tab. Select only the scopes required by the endpoints and enabled features. App Folder limits where the app can act; it does not grant file actions by itself. Request `files.content.write` only when the agent must create, edit, move, or delete files. Add collaboration scopes only when that feature is enabled.

sources.quote: The scope required for any given API call is documented on the endpoint:
Requesting more scope and content access than required may result in end users not accepting your OAuth request and could impact your app review process.

detail.text: Open Settings, then OAuth 2. Add a fixed callback URI. Use HTTPS except for localhost during local testing. Send the exact registered URI in authorization requests. Do not accept customer-provided callback URLs.

sources.quote: This must be the exact URI registered under OAuth 2 on your app’s Settings tab in the Developer Console

steps.title: Draft the callback handler

detail.text: Use authorization-code flow with offline access. Bind one-time state to the signed-in user and intended route. Store tokens separately for each connected Dropbox account. For a confidential server-side app, authenticate the token exchange with the app key and secret. Use a PKCE verifier for a client that cannot safely retain the app secret.

sources.quote: https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token
This parameter should be used to protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

steps.output:
GET /oauth/dropbox/callback:
1. Load and consume state from encrypted storage.
2. Reject expired, missing, or user-mismatched state.
3. Verify the PKCE verifier binding.
4. Exchange code at https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token.
5. Encrypt refresh_token by connected account.
6. Store expires_at from expires_in.
7. Redirect only to the stored return route.

detail.text: Use your developer account first. Add permitted test users in the Console. Test consent, refresh, disconnect, and each requested file action.

sources.quote: Click Generate access token to automatically complete app authorization against your Dropbox account and get an access token you can start using immediately for testing.
Dropbox API Explorer

detail.text: If the agent syncs changes, add a public HTTPS webhook in Settings. During webhook verification, echo Dropbox’s `challenge`. For notifications, verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body, return within 10 seconds, and process events asynchronously.

sources.quote: On your app’s Settings tab, enter the full URI for your webhook
Every notification request will include a header called X-Dropbox-Signature that includes an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body, using your app secret as the signing key.

steps.title: Prepare review answers

detail.text: Prepare a short use-case explanation. Explain every scope and Full Dropbox need. State how users consent to AI processing and how tokens are protected.

sources.quote: you’ll be prompted to supply additional information such as how your app uses the API.
only access, store, transfer and process User Data in accordance with Users’ instructions, including a Developer App’s configuration settings

steps.output:
Use case: The agent reads only user-approved Dropbox files to answer user requests.
Data use: File content is sent to an AI provider only after clear user consent.
Scopes: We request metadata and content scopes only for enabled features.
Security: Tokens are encrypted and access is separated by connected account.
Branding: We do not imply Dropbox endorsement.

detail.text: Add an app icon and privacy policy. In Settings, select Apply for production. If below 50 linked users, complete Request early review with evidence and a detailed reason.

sources.quote: please provide evidence and a detailed explanation under the Request early review field
Be sure to include a clear privacy policy that’s specific to your app and describes what your app will and won’t do with user data.

detail.text: Wait for Dropbox's production-readiness decision. This reported timing is not a service-level commitment. Resubmit after fixing any feedback.

sources.quote: We generally get to all production requests within a few business days.
Your app will undergo a production readiness review by Dropbox and will either be approved or denied.

detail.text: After approval, enable the Connect Dropbox flow for customers. Ask for extra scopes later when users enable features needing them. Refresh access tokens before background jobs.

sources.quote: you may also ask for minimal permissions at authorization time - then re-authorize at later time if and when your application requires more permissions from the user.
This request won’t return a new refresh token since refresh tokens don’t expire automatically and can be reused repeatedly.

gotchas.text: Do not use the legacy implicit token flow for background agent work. Request offline access so Dropbox returns a refresh token.

sources.quote: However, response_type=token is considered legacy and no longer recommended.
then the access token payload returned by a successful /oauth2/token call will contain a short-lived access_token and a long-lived refresh_token

sources.quote: Developers will need to direct a Dropbox Business team administrator through the standard OAuth 2.0 flow to install their application on a Dropbox Business team.

sources.quote: please provide evidence and a detailed explanation under the Request early review field

sources.quote: If you can't find an answer in the resources above, you can contact API support .
could you open a Dropbox API support ticket so our team can discuss your use case in more detail?

whenBlocked.text: If review is denied, apply the feedback, correct the app, and resubmit the production request.

sources.quote: Your app will undergo a production readiness review by Dropbox and will either be approved or denied.
